sanskrit: agne sahantan ā bhara dyumnasya prāsahā rayim | viśvā yaś carṣaṇīr abhy āsā vājeṣu sāsahat ||
english: O Agni, bring hither the wealth of brilliance that overcomes all — that wealth which shall conquer all peoples at its encounter and prevail in the contests.

sanskrit: tam agne pṛtanāṣahaṁ rayiṁ sahasva ā bhara | tvaṁ hi satyo adbhuto dātā vājasya gomataḥ ||
english: Bring here that battle-conquering wealth, O Agni; for you are the true, the wonderful, the bestower of food-prize along with cattle.

sanskrit: viśve hi tvā sajoṣaso janāso vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | hotāraṁ sadmasu priyaṁ vyanti vāryā puru ||
english: For all the peoples of one mind, who have strewn the sacred grass, seek you as the dear Hotr in their dwellings and win many desirable goods.

sanskrit: sa hi ṣmā viśvacarṣaṇir abhimāti saho dadhe | agna eṣu kṣayeṣv ā revan naḥ śukra dīdihi dyumat pāvaka dīdihi ||
english: For he, the all-people's champion, has assumed the might that overwhelms the foe. O Agni, shine for us with brilliance in these abodes, O gleaming one, shine with radiance, O Purifier.

sanskrit: agne tvaṁ no antama uta trātā śivo bhavā varūthyaḥ ||
english: O Agni, be our nearest kin, our protector; be gracious and our shelter.

sanskrit: vasur agnir vasuśravā acchā nakṣi dyumattamaṁ rayiṁ dāḥ ||
english: Agni is good, renowned for good things; draw near and grant wealth most glorious.

sanskrit: sa no bodhi śrudhī havam uruṣyā ṇo aghāyataḥ samasmāt ||
english: So be wakeful for us, hear our call, protect us from every adversary who would harm us.

sanskrit: taṁ tvā śociṣṭha dīdivaḥ sumnāya nūnam īmahe sakhibhyaḥ ||
english: You who shine most brilliantly, O Agni, we now implore you for favour — for the sake of our friends.

sanskrit: acchā vo agnim avase devaṁ gāsi sa no vasuḥ | rāsat putra ṛṣūṇām ṛtāvā parṣati dviṣaḥ ||
english: I approach Agni, your divine one, for protection; he is our treasure. The son of the seers who holds the truth bestows gifts and carries us beyond our foes.

sanskrit: sa hi satyo yam pūrve cid devāsaś cid yam īdhire | hotāram mandrajihvam it sudītibhi vibhāvasum ||
english: He is the true one whom even the ancient gods kindled as the Hotr with the honey-tongued flame — him who shines everywhere with riches and bright splendour.

sanskrit: sa no dhītī variṣṭhayā śreṣṭhayā ca sumatyā | agne rāyo didīhi naḥ suvṛktibhir vareṇya ||
english: With the highest, the best thought, and with good mind, O Agni the most desirable, shine upon us with wealth, with fair hymns.

sanskrit: agnir deveṣu rājaty agnir marteṣv āviśan | agnir no havyavāhano 'gniṁ dhībhiḥ saparyata ||
english: Agni reigns among the gods; Agni enters among mortals; Agni is our carrier of oblations — worship Agni with thoughts.

sanskrit: agnis tuviśravastamamṁ tuvibrahāṇam uttamam | atūrtaṁ śrāvayatpatim putraṁ dadāti dāśuṣe ||
english: Agni bestows on the pious worshipper a son of most mighty fame, of great prayer-power, supreme — an unsurpassed lord, renowned for glory.

sanskrit: agnir dadāti satpatiṁ sāsāha yo yudhā nṛbhiḥ | agnir atyaṁ raghuṣyadaṁ jetāram aparājitam ||
english: Agni grants a true lord who has overcome enemies in battle with his men — a swift steed, a conqueror, never defeated.

sanskrit: yad vāhiṣṭhaṁ tad agnaye bṛhad arca vibhāvaso | mahīṣīva tvad rayis tvad vājā ud īrate ||
english: Sing the loudest praise to Agni, a great hymn, O Vibhāvasu; like a great cow from you comes wealth, from you prizes rise up.

sanskrit: tava dyumanto arcayo grāvocyate bṛhat | uto te tanyatur yathā svāno arta tmanā divaḥ ||
english: Your radiant flames are called forth with a great hymn at the pressing-stone; and your thundering, like the spontaneous roar of heaven, resounds of itself.

sanskrit: evām̐ agniṁ vasūyavaḥ sahasānanaṁ vavandima | sa no viśvā ati dviṣaḥ parṣan nāveva sukratuḥ ||
english: Thus we have praised Agni, the ever-victorious, we who long for riches. May he, of good resolve, carry us across all our foes, as if in a ship.

sanskrit: agne pāvaka rociṣā mandrayā deva jihvayā | ā devān vakṣi yakṣi ca ||
english: O Agni the purifier, with your shining, joyful, divine tongue, bring hither the gods and offer sacrifice.

sanskrit: taṁ tvā ghṛtasnav īmahe citrabhāno svardṛśam | devām̐ ā vītaye vaha ||
english: You who are bright with clarified butter, O Agni of wonderful radiance, beholder of heaven — bring the gods for our enjoyment.

sanskrit: vītihotraṁ tvā kave dyumantaṁ sam idhīmahi | agne bṛhantam adhvare ||
english: O wise Agni, we kindle you, the inviter of gods to the feast, the radiant, the great, at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: agne viśvebhir ā gahi devebhir havyadātaye | hotāraṁ tvā vṛṇīmahe ||
english: Come, O Agni, with all the gods, for the giving of oblations; we choose you as the Hotr.

sanskrit: yajamānāya sunvata āgne suvīryaṁ vaha | devair ā satsi barhiṣi ||
english: O Agni, bring manly vigour to the worshipper who presses Soma; sit with the gods on the sacred grass.

sanskrit: samidhānaḥ sahasrajid agne dharmāṇi puṣyasi | devānāṁ dūta ukthyaḥ ||
english: When kindled, O Agni, conqueror of thousands, you nourish the ordinances of the gods; you are the messenger of the gods, worthy of hymns.

sanskrit: ny agniṁ jātavedasaṁ hotravāhaṁ yaviṣṭhyam | dadhātā devam ṛtvijam ||
english: Establish Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of oblations, the youngest, the divine priest of the season.

sanskrit: pra yajña etv ānuṣag adyā devavyacastamaḥ | stṛṇīta barhir āsade ||
english: Let the sacrifice go forward today in orderly sequence, most pleasing to the gods; spread the sacred grass for the seating.

sanskrit: edam maruto aśvinā mitraḥ sīdantu varuṇaḥ | devāsaḥ sarvayā viśā ||
english: Here may the Maruts, the Aśvins, Mitra and Varuṇa sit — all the gods with every clan.

sanskrit: anasvantā satpatir māmhe me gāvā cetiṣṭho asuro maghonaḥ | traivṛṣṇo agne daśabhiḥ sahasrair vaiśvānara tryaruṇaś ciketa ||
english: The true lord gave me gifts — wealth in cattle and in draught-animals — the most attentive, the mighty, the generous one. Tryaruṇa of the Traivṛṣṇa family has recognised you, O Agni Vaiśvānara, with ten thousands.

sanskrit: yo me śatā ca viṁśatiṁ ca gonāṁ harī ca yuktā sudhurā dadāti | vaiśvānara suṣṭuto vāvṛdhāno 'gne yaccha tryaruṇāya śarma ||
english: He who has given me a hundred and twenty cows and two well-yoked tawny steeds of good draught — O Agni Vaiśvānara, well-praised and ever waxing, extend your shelter to Tryaruṇa.

sanskrit: evā te agne sumatiṁ cakāno naviṣṭhāya navamaṁ trasadasyuḥ | yo me giras tuvijātasya pūrvīr yuktenābhi tryaruṇo gṛṇāti ||
english: Thus Trasadasyu, seeking your favour, has made this newest hymn for you, O Agni; Tryaruṇa, yoked with purpose, praises with many praises my songs addressed to you of mighty birth.

sanskrit: yo ma iti pravocaty aśvameddhāya sūraye | dadad ṛcā saniṁ yate dadad medhām ṛtāyate ||
english: He who proclaims 'this is mine' — giving through the hymn to the inspired lord at the horse-sacrifice — bestows the prize on the seeker, bestows wisdom on him who follows the truth.

sanskrit: yasya mā paruṣāḥ śatam uddharṣayanti ukṣaṇaḥ | aśvamedhasya dānāḥ somā iva tryāśiraḥ ||
english: A hundred spotted bulls rouse me with delight — the gifts of the horse-sacrifice are like Soma mixed threefold.

sanskrit: indrāgnī śatadāvny aśvamedhe suvīryam | kṣatraṁ dhārayatam bṛhad divi sūryam ivājaram ||
english: O Indrā and Agni, at the horse-sacrifice of a hundred gifts, uphold heroic strength and sovereignty, great and undecaying as the sun in heaven.

sanskrit: samiddho agnir divi śocir aśret pratyaṅṅ uṣasam urviyā vi bhāti | eti prācī viśvavārā namobhir devām̐ īḻānā haviṣā ghṛtācī ||
english: The kindled Agni has stretched his flame to heaven, shining broadly to meet the Dawn. The all-desirable one comes eastward with obeisances, seeking the gods with an oblation of clarified butter.

sanskrit: samidhyamāno amṛtasya rājasi haviṣ kṛṇvantaṁ sacase svastaye | viśvaṁ sa dhatte draviṇaṁ yam invasy ātithyam agne ni ca dhatta it puraḥ ||
english: Being kindled, you rule over the immortal realm; you accompany him who prepares the oblation, for his welfare. He gains all wealth whom you impel, O Agni; yet place the guest-offering first of all.

sanskrit: agne śardha mahaṭe saubhagāya tava dyumnāny uttamāni santu | saṁ jāspatyaṁ suyamam ā kṛṇuṣva śatrūyatām abhi tiṣṭhā mahāṁsi ||
english: O Agni, exert your might for great felicity; let your glories be highest. Bring about good mastery over the household; tread down the great powers of those who act as foes.

sanskrit: samiḍdhasya pramahaso 'gne vande tava śriyam | vṛṣabho dyumnavām̐ asi sam adhvareṣu idhyase ||
english: O Agni, kindled and of great might, I praise your splendour; you are a bull of radiance, kindled together at the sacrifices.

sanskrit: samiddho agna āhuta devān yakṣi svadhvara | tvaṁ hi havyavāḻ asi ||
english: Kindled, O Agni, supplied with oblations, worship the gods at the well-performed sacrifice; for you are indeed the carrier of oblations.

sanskrit: ā juhotā duvasyatāgnim prayaty adhvare | vṛṇīdhvaṁ havyavāhanam ||
english: Pour the oblation; serve Agni at the advancing sacrifice; choose him as the carrier of oblations.

sanskrit: try aryamā manuṣo devatātā trī rocanā divyā dhārayanta | arcanti tvā marutaḥ pūtadakṣās tvam eṣām ṛṣir indrāsi dhīraḥ ||
english: Three are the divine ranks of Aryamā among humans; three are the luminous realms of heaven which they uphold. The Maruts of purified might praise you; you, O Indra, are their seer, the wise one.

sanskrit: anu yad īm maruto mandasānam ārcann indraṁ papivāṁsaṁ sutasya | ādatta vajram abhi yad ahiṁ hann apo yahvīr asṛjat sartavā u ||
english: When the Maruts praised Indra rejoicing, when he had drunk of the pressed Soma — he seized the thunderbolt with which he smote the serpent, and set the great waters free to flow.

sanskrit: uta brahmāṇo maruto me asyendra somāsya suṣutasya peyāḥ | tad dhi havyam manuṣe gā avindad ahan ahim papivām̐ indro asya ||
english: And the singer-priests — the Maruts — were mine, O Indra; you drank of the well-pressed Soma. That was indeed the oblation for mortal man; Indra, having drunk thereof, found the cows and smote the serpent.

sanskrit: ād rodasī vitaraṁ vi ṣkabhāyat saṁvivyānaś cid bhiyase mṛgaṁ kaḥ | jigartim indro apajargurahāṇaḥ prati śvasantam ava dānavam han ||
english: He propped apart the two worlds more widely; who would frighten the beast that had wrapped itself around? Indra, roaring, struck down the swallower — he smote the Dānava that hissed against him.

sanskrit: adha kratvā maghavan tubhyaṁ devā anu viśve adaduḥ somapeyyam | yat sūryasya haritaḥ patantīḥ puraḥ satīr uparā etaśe kaḥ ||
english: Then, O bountiful Indra, by your might all the gods gave you the right to drink Soma; for who could stand before the tawny steeds of the sun, the upper ones set before Etaśa?

sanskrit: nava yad asya navatiṁ ca bhogān sākaṁ vajreṇa maghavā vivṛścat | arcantīndram marutaḥ sadhasthe traiṣṭubhena vacasā bādhata dyām ||
english: When the bountiful one with his thunderbolt cut off at once the ninety-nine coils of the serpent, the Maruts praised Indra at the gathering and with Triṣṭubh speech they pressed against heaven.

sanskrit: sakhā sakhye apacat tūyam agnir asya kratvā mahiṣā trī śatāni | trī sākaṁ indro manuṣaḥ sarāṁsi sutam pibad vṛtrahatyāya somam ||
english: A friend cooked swiftly for a friend — Agni by his will cooked three hundred buffaloes; Indra at one time drank the three lakes of pressed Soma of Manu's folk for the slaying of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: trī yac chatā mahiṣāṇāṁ agho māstrī sarāṁsi maghavā somyāpāḥ | kāraṁ na viśve ahvanta devā bharam indrāya yad ahiṁ jaghāna ||
english: When the bountiful Soma-drinker consumed three hundred buffaloes and three lakes — all the gods called it a great deed and brought it as tribute to Indra when he slew the serpent.

sanskrit: uśanā yat sahasyair ayātaṁ gṛham indra jūjuvānebhir aśvaiḥ | vanvāno atra sarathaṁ yayātha kutsena devair avaṇor ha śuṣṇam ||
english: When you came, O Indra, with Uśanā and with swiftly rushing steeds to his house, you rode there in the same chariot, winning; with Kutsa and the gods you indeed warded off Śuṣṇa.

sanskrit: prānyac cakram avṛhaḥ sūryasya kutsāyānyad varivo yātave 'kaḥ | anāso dasyūm̐r amṛṇo vadhena ni duryone āvṛṇaṅ mṛdhravācaḥ ||
english: You tore away one wheel of the sun's chariot; for Kutsa you made the other free to move. You crushed the noseless Dasyus with your weapon and penned up the foul-speakers in their dark abode.

sanskrit: stomāsas tvā gaurivīter avardhann arandhayo vaidathinaya piprum | ā tvām ṛjiśvā sakhyāya cakre pacan paktīr apibhaḥ somam asya ||
english: The hymns of Gaurivīti increased you; you gave Pipru into the power of Vaidathin's son. Ṛjiśvā enlisted you in friendship; while he was cooking the offerings you drank his Soma.

sanskrit: navagvāsaḥ sutasomāsa indraṁ daśagvāso abhy arcantyu arkaiḥ | gavyaṁ cid ūrvam apidhānavantaṁ taṁ cin naraḥ śaśamānā apa vran ||
english: The Navagvas with pressed Soma, the Daśagvas with their hymns, praise Indra. The men who had laboured together drove open the pen of cows, though it was closed with a covering.

sanskrit: katho nu te pari carāṇi vidvān vīryā maghavan yā cakartha | yā co nu navyā kṛṇavaḥ śaviṣṭha pred u tā te vidatheṣu bravāma ||
english: How shall I worthily celebrate your heroic deeds, O bountiful Indra, those you have done? And what new feats you will yet do, O mightiest — those too we shall proclaim at the assemblies.

sanskrit: etā viśvā cakṛvām̐ indra bhūry aparīto januṣā vīryeṇa | yā cin nu vajrin kṛṇavo dadhrṣvān na te vartā taviṣyā asti tasyāḥ ||
english: Having done all these many things, O Indra, unrestrained in birth and in might — whatever you, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bold, shall yet do — there is none to withstand that power of yours.

sanskrit: indra brahma kriyamāṇā juṣasva yā te śaviṣṭha navyā akarma | vasreva bhadrā sukṛtā vasūyū rathaṁ na dhīraḥ svapā atakṣam ||
english: O Indra, mightiest, accept the prayers being made — the new ones we have fashioned for you. Like a skilled craftsman who has made a fine, well-wrought garment, the wise artisan has fashioned this as one might make a chariot.

sanskrit: kva sya vīraḥ ko apaśyad indraṁ sukharatham īyamānaṁ haribhyām | yo rāyā vajrī sutasomam icchan tad oko gantā puruhūta ūtī ||
english: Where is that hero? Who has seen Indra riding comfortably in his chariot drawn by the tawny horses? He who, the thunderer, with wealth seeks the pressed Soma — he the much-invoked will come to that home, with his aid.

sanskrit: avācacakṣam padam asya sasvar ugraṁ nidhātur anv āyam icchan | apṛccham anyām̐ uta te ma āhur indraṁ naro bubudhānā aśema ||
english: I have looked southward at his resounding place of the fierce treasure-keeper, seeking my way; I asked others, and they said the same to me: may we attain to Indra, O men, when awake.

sanskrit: pra nu vayaṁ sute yā te kṛtānīndra bravāma yāni no jujoṣaḥ | vedad avidvāñ chṛṇavac ca vidvān vahate 'yam maghavā sarvasenāḥ ||
english: Now at the pressing we proclaim, O Indra, those deeds of yours which you have favoured in us. Let the unknowing know, let the knowing hear: this bountiful one commands all armies.

sanskrit: sthiram manaś cakṛṣe jāta indra veṣīd eko yudhaye bhūyasaś cit | aśmānaṁ cic chavasā didyuto vi vido gavām ūrvam usriyāṇām ||
english: At your birth, O Indra, you made your mind firm; alone you were fain to fight against multitudes. Even the stone you split with your might and found the stall of the cows, the luminous ones.

sanskrit: paro yat tvam parama ājanīṣṭhāḥ parāvati śrutyaṁ nāma bibhrat | ataś cid indrād abhayanta devā viśvā apo ajayad dāsapatnīḥ ||
english: When you were born the highest one in the highest sphere, bearing a name renowned in the far distance — even then the gods were afraid of Indra; he won all waters under whose dominion were the Dāsas.

sanskrit: tubhyed ete marutaḥ suśevā arcantyu arkam sunvantyu andhaḥ | ahim ohānam apa āśayānam pra māyābhir māyinaṁ sakṣad indraḥ ||
english: For you these gracious Maruts sing the hymn and press the Soma-juice. The serpent that lay blocking the waters — Indra shall overcome with his powers of māyā that māyā-wielding one.

sanskrit: vi ṣū mṛdho januṣā dānam invan ahan gavā maghavan saṁcakānaḥ | atrā dāsasya namuce śiro yad avartayo manave gātum icchan ||
english: Scattering enemies by birth, driving forth the gift, you, O bountiful one, desiring to win cattle, rolled away the head of the Dāsa Namuci there, seeking a path for Manu.

sanskrit: yujam hi mām akṛthā ād id indra śiro dāsasya namucer mathāyan | aśmānaṁ cit svaryam vartamānam pra cakriyeva rodasī marudbhyaḥ ||
english: For you made me your ally, O Indra, churning off the head of Namuci the Dāsa; even the sun-stone rolling along you rolled as if on wheels between the two worlds for the Maruts.

sanskrit: striyo hi dāsa āyudhāni cakre kim mā karann abalā asya senāḥ | antar hy akhyad ubhe asya dhene athopa praid yudhaye dasyum indraḥ ||
english: The Dāsa Namuci had made weapons out of women; what could his feeble armies do to me? For Indra saw both his milk-cows and then went forth to battle against the Dasyu.

sanskrit: sam atra gāvo 'bhito 'navante iheha vatsair viyutā yad āsan | saṁ tā indro asṛjad asya śākair yad īṁ somāsaḥ suṣutā amandan ||
english: The cows lowed on all sides here when they were separated from their calves; Indra let them go with his powers when the well-pressed Somas gladdened him.

sanskrit: yad īṁ somā babhrūdhūtā amanda naro ravīd vṛṣabhaḥ sādaneṣu | purandharaḥ papivām̐ indro asya punar gavām adadād usriyāṇām ||
english: When the tawny-shaken Somas had delighted him, the bull bellowed among the dwellings; Indra the city-breaker, having drunk, gave back to him the cows, the luminous ones.

sanskrit: bhadram idaṁ ruśamā agne akran gavāṁ catvāri dadataḥ sahasrā | ṛṇaṁcayasya prayatā maghāni praty agrabhīṣma nṛtamasya nṛṇām ||
english: The Ruśamas have done this good thing for Agni, giving four thousand cows; we have received the ample gifts of Ṛṇaṁcaya, the bravest of heroes.

sanskrit: supeśasam māva sṛjanty astaṁ gavāṁ sahasrair ruśamāso agne | tīvrā indram amamanduḥ sutāso 'ktor vyuṣṭau paritakmyāyāḥ ||
english: The Ruśamas send me home adorned with many ornaments, with thousands of cows, O Agni; the potent pressed Somas have exhilarated Indra at the night's dawning of that Paritakmyā.

sanskrit: auchat sā rātrī paritakmyā yām̐ ṛṇaṁcaye rājani ruśamānām | atyo na vājī raghur ajyamāno babḥruś catvāry asanat sahasrā ||
english: That night of the Paritakmyā shone bright — the night in which the Ruśamas were under king Ṛṇaṁcaya; swift as a racing steed urged on, the tawny one won four thousands.

sanskrit: catuḥsahasraṁ gavyasya paśvaḥ praty agrabhīṣma ruśameṣv agne | gharmaś cit taptaḥ pravṛje ya āsīd ayasmayo tam v ādāma viprāḥ ||
english: Four thousand cattle we have received among the Ruśamas, O Agni; even the heated metal pot that stood at the libation-place — that we, the wise, have taken.

sanskrit: indro rathāya pravataṁ kṛṇoti yam adhyasthān maghavā vājayantam | yūtheva paśvo vy unoti gopā ariṣṭo yāti prathamaḥ siṣāsan ||
english: Indra makes a downward slope for the chariot on which the bountiful one has mounted, eager for booty; like a herdsman unfolding a herd of cattle, he goes first, uninjured, seeking to win.

sanskrit: ā pra drava harivo mā vi venaḥ piśaṅgarāte abhi naḥ sacasva | na hi tvad indra vasyo anyad asty amenām̐ś cij janivathaś cakartha ||
english: Come running hither, O lord of tawny horses; do not stray away, O red-giving one; be with us. For there is nothing better than you, O Indra; even the blameless you have made to have wives.

sanskrit: ud yat sahaḥ sahasa ājaniṣṭa dediṣṭa indra indriyāṇi viśvā | prācodayat sudughā vavre antar vi jyotiṣā saṁvavṛtvat tamo 'vaḥ ||
english: When might was born from might, O Indra, all the faculties of Indra flashed forth; he drove forward the good milch-cows within the enclosure and rolled away the darkness below with his light.

sanskrit: anavas te ratham aśvāya takṣan tvaṣṭā vajram puruhūta dyumantam | brahmāṇa indram mahayanto arkair avardayann ahaye hantavā u ||
english: The Anus fashioned the chariot for your horse, O much-invoked; Tvaṣṭṛ made the shining thunderbolt; the prayer-priests, magnifying Indra with hymns, increased him for the slaying of the serpent.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇe yat te vṛṣaṇo arkam arcān indra grāvāṇo aditiḥ sajoṣāḥ | anaśvāso ye pavayo 'rathā indreṣitā abhy avartanta dasyūn ||
english: When the pressing-stones, and Aditi joined together, sang the hymn to you the bull, O Indra — they without horses, without chariots, yet impelled by Indra, turned against the Dasyus.

sanskrit: pra te pūrvāṇi karaṇāni vocam pra nūtanā maghavan yā cakartha | śaktīvo yad vibharā rodasī ubhe jayan apo manave dānucitrāḥ ||
english: I will proclaim your former deeds, and the new ones, O bountiful one, that you have done — when, O Śakti's scion, bearing both worlds you won the bright-showering waters for Manu.

sanskrit: tad in nu te karaṇaṁ dasma viprāhiṁ yad ghnann ojo atrāmimīthāḥ | śuṣṇasya cit pari māyā agṛbhṇāḥ prapitvaṁ yann apa dasyūm̐r asedhaḥ ||
english: That indeed is your wondrous deed, O sage hero — that slaying the serpent you measured your might here; you grasped even Śuṣṇa's illusory powers, and going at the right time you drove away the Dasyus.

sanskrit: tvam apo yadave turvaśāyāramayaḥ sudughāḥ pāra indra | ugram ayātam avahos ha kutsaṁ saṁ ha yad vām uśanāranta devāḥ ||
english: You brought the good milch-cows to rest on the bank, O Indra, for Yadu and Turvaśa; you carried mighty Kutsa across when the gods and Uśanā had allied with you both.

sanskrit: indrākutsā vahamānā rathena vām atyā api karṇe vahantu | niḥ ṣīm adbhyo dhamantho niḥ ṣadhasthān maghono hṛdo varathastamāṁsi ||
english: O Indra and Kutsa, being carried in the chariot, let the racing steeds carry you both ear to ear. You blew the darkness out of the waters, out of the dwelling-places, out of the heart of the bountiful one.

sanskrit: vātasya yuktān suyujaś cid aśvān kaviś cid eṣo ajagann avasyuḥ | viśve te atra marutaḥ sakhāya indra brahmāṇi taviṣīm avardhan ||
english: Even the well-yoked horses that were yoked to the wind — even that seer came here seeking help. Here all the Maruts are your allies, O Indra; with prayers they increased your might.

sanskrit: sūraś cid rathaṁ paritakmyāyām pūrvaṁ karo 'aparaṁ jūjuvāṁsam | bharac cakram etaśaḥ saṁ riṇāti puro dadhat saniṣyati kratuṁ naḥ ||
english: Even the sun made his chariot as the first in the Paritakmyā race, having already outstripped the latter; the steed Etaśa rolls the wheel forward; setting prizes before, he will win our desire.

sanskrit: āyaṁ janā abhicakṣe jagāmendra sakhāyaṁ sutasomam icchan | vadan grāvāva vedim bhriyāte yasya jīram adhvaryavaś caranti ||
english: He has come here, O peoples, for Indra to behold, seeking his friend with pressed Soma; resounding like the pressing-stones, the altar is to be served — for him whose nimble priests are in motion.

sanskrit: ye cākananta cākananta nū te martā amṛta mo te aṁha āran | vāvandhiyajyūm̐r uta teṣu dhehy ojo janeṣu yeṣu te syāma ||
english: Those who have delighted and who now delight — O immortal one, may no affliction reach those mortals! Cherish the sacrificers who praise you; place your strength among those peoples among whom we would be.

sanskrit: adardar utsam asṛjo vi khāni tvam arṇavān badbadhānām̐ aramaṇāḥ | mahāntam indra parvataṁ vi yad vaḥ sṛjo vi dhārā ava dānavam han ||
english: You burst open the spring, you released the caverns; you set the seas free from their confinement. When you cleft the great mountain, O Indra, you released the streams and smote the Dānava downward.

sanskrit: tvam utsām̐ ṛtubhir badbadhānām̐ araṁha ūdhaḥ parvatasya vajrin | ahiṁ cid ugra prayutaṁ śayānaṁ jaghanvām̐ indra taviṣīm adhatthāḥ ||
english: You, O thunderer, set free the springs, confined by the seasons, the udder of the mountain. Even the serpent lying sent forth, O fierce Indra, you smote — and put forth your might.

sanskrit: tyasya cin mahato nir mṛgasya vadhar jaghāna taviṣībhir indraḥ | ya eka id apratir manyamāna ād asmād anyo ajaniṣṭa tavyān ||
english: Even of that great beast Indra struck the weapon down with his powers — he who, thinking himself alone and unrivalled, was surpassed by one mightier than him who was born after.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid eṣāṁ svadhayā madantam miho napātaṁ suvṛdhaṁ tamogām | vṛṣaprabharmā dānavasya bhāmaṁ vajreṇa vajrī ni jaghāna śuṣṇam ||
english: Even that one among them rejoicing in his own power — the son of the cloud-mist, the well-grown, the darkness-going — him, Śuṣṇa, the fierce one of the Dānava, the thunderer slew with his thunderbolt, the bull bearing it along.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid asya kratubhir niṣattam amarmaṇo vidad id asya marma | yad īṁ sukṣatra prabhṛtā madasya yuyutsantaṁ tamasi harmye dhāḥ ||
english: Even him who through his own designs sat firm, the seemingly invulnerable — Indra found the vulnerable spot in him. When, O lord of good rule, with the outpoured exhilaration, you placed the fighting one in darkness within his stronghold.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid itthā katpayaṁ śayānam asūrye tamasi vāvṛdhānam | taṁ cin mandāno vṛṣabhaḥ sutasyo 'ccair indro apagūryā jaghāna ||
english: Even him lying in such a pitiful state, growing great in sunless darkness — him indeed the bull Indra, exhilarated by the pressed Soma, struck down with a shout from on high.

sanskrit: ud yad indro mahate dānavāya vadhar yamiṣṭa saho apratītam | yad īṁ vajrasya prabhṛtau dadābha viśvasya jantor adhamaṁ cakāra ||
english: When Indra raised the irresistible weapon of might against the great Dānava — when in the wielding of the thunderbolt he shattered him — he made the lowest of all creatures.

sanskrit: tyaṁ cid arṇaṁ madhupaṁ śayānam asinvaṁ vavram mahy ādad ugraḥ | apādam atraṁ mahatā vadhena ni duryone āvṛṇaṅ mṛdhravācam ||
english: Even that ocean-honey-drinker lying there, unsent — the fierce one seized that great cave; he penned up the footless devourer with a great weapon, the foul-spoken one, in his dark abode.

sanskrit: ko asya śuṣmaṁ taviṣīṁ varāta eko dhanā bharate 'pratītaḥ | ime cid asya jrayaso nu devī indrasyaujaso bhiyasā jihāte ||
english: Who would restrain his impetuous might? Alone, unrestrained, he carries off the prizes. Even these two divine expanses now — the two worlds — recoil from the force of Indra in fear.

sanskrit: ny asmai devī svadhitir jihīta indrāya gātur uśatīva yeme | saṁ yad ojo yuvate viśvam ābhir anu svadhāvne kṣitayo namanta ||
english: The divine axe turned for him; it yearned toward Indra like a willing one seeking the path. When all might joined itself together with these two, the peoples bowed to the self-powerful one.

sanskrit: ekaṁ nu tvā satpatim pāñcajanyaṁ jātaṁ śṛṇomi yaśasaṁ janeṣu | tam me jagṛbhra āśaso naviṣṭhaṁ doṣā vastor havamānāsa indram ||
english: I hear of one true lord born to all five peoples, famous among them; let those hopes of mine seize him most recently — those who call upon Indra by night and by day.

sanskrit: evā hi tvām ṛtuthā yātayantam maghā viprebhyo dadataṁ śṛṇomi | kiṁ te brahmāṇo gṛhate sakhāyo ye tvāyā nidadhuḥ kāmam indra ||
english: For thus I hear of you, ordering things in proper season, giving gifts to the wise-men in abundance. What do your priest-friends receive, those who have placed their desire in you, O Indra?

sanskrit: mahi mahe tavase dīdhye nṝn indrāyetthā tavase atatvyān | yo asmai sumatiṁ vājasātau stuto jane samarYaś ciketa ||
english: I have thought deeply on behalf of great and mighty men, thus for Indra the mighty beyond measure; he who is praised among people, who notices those who seek his favour in the gaining of prizes.

sanskrit: sa tvaṁ na indra dhiyasāno arkair harīṇāṁ vṛṣan yoktram aśreḥ | yā itthā maghavann anu joṣam vakṣo abhi prāryaḥ sakṣi janān ||
english: You, O Indra, being praised with hymns and songs, have yoked the strap of the tawny horses, O bull. You who thus, O bountiful one, following their wish pressed forward — overcome the peoples before you.

sanskrit: na te ta indrābhy asmad ṛṣvāyuktāso abrahmāṭā yad asan | tiṣṭhā ratham adhi taṁ vajrahastā raśmiṁ deva yamase svaśvaḥ ||
english: Those tall ones harnessed from your side against us, O Indra — they would be prayerless. Stand upon that chariot, O thunderbolt-handed one; you hold the rein, O god of good horses.

sanskrit: purū yat ta indra santy ukthā gave cakarthorvarāsu yudhyan | tatakṣe sūryāya cid okasi sve vṛṣā samatsu dāsasya nāma cit ||
english: Many praises there are of you, O Indra; fighting for cows you have carved out the plains. The bull fashioned even a dwelling for the sun and blotted out even the name of the Dāsa in battles.

sanskrit: vayaṁ te ta indra ye ca naraḥ śardho jajñānā yātāś ca rathāḥ | āsmāñ jagamyād ahiśuṣma satvā bhago na havyaḥ prabhṛtheṣu cāruḥ ||
english: We and those men, O Indra, the troop that has arisen, and the chariots that have set forth — may the hero of serpent-power come to us; like Bhaga, to be invoked and lovely at the offertories.

sanskrit: papṛkṣeṇyam indra tve hy ojo nṛmṇāni ca nṛtamāno amartaḥ | sa na enīṁ vasavāno rayiṁ dāḥ prāryaḥ stuṣe tuvimaghasya dānam ||
english: In you, O Indra, is the excellently mixed might, and the manly forces — you the most manly, the immortal. Provide us with shining wealth, clothed in good things; I praise the gift of the greatly bountiful one.

sanskrit: evā na indrotibhir ava pāhi gṛṇataḥ śūra kārūn | uta tvacaṁ dadato vājasātau piprīhi madhvaḥ suṣutasya cāroḥ ||
english: Thus protect us, O Indra, with your aids — those who sing your praises, O hero; and in the winning of prizes, gratify the Kārus who give their own skin, with the sweet well-pressed Soma so lovely.

sanskrit: uta tye mā paururkutsyasya sūres trasadasyur hiraṇino rarāṇāḥ | vahantu mā daśa śyetāso asya gairikṣitasya kratubhir nu saśce ||
english: And those tawny gifts of the hero Trasadasyu of Purukutsa's lineage, shining with gold, have rewarded me; may ten white horses of the Gairikṣita carry me — I have now followed his designs.

sanskrit: uta tye mā mārutāśvasya śoṇāḥ kratvāmaghāso vidathasya rātau | sahasrā me cyavatāno dadāna ānūkam aryo vapuṣe nārcat ||
english: And those red steeds of Mārutāśva, mighty in designs and generous, at the award of the assembly — giving me thousands in cascades — the lord has not adorned his body with any equal gift.

sanskrit: uta tye mā dhvanyasya juṣṭā lakṣmaṇyasya surucoyo yatānāḥ | mahnā rāyaḥ saṁvaraṇasya ṛṣer vrajam na gāvaḥ prayatā api gman ||
english: And those beloved brightly-shining steeds of Dhvanya Lakṣmaṇa, setting forth — they have come to me through the greatness of the seer Saṁvaraṇa's wealth, like cows going forth into the pen.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrum ajarā svarvaty anu svadhāmitā dasmam īyate | sunotana pacata brahmavāhase puruṣṭutāya prataraṁ dadhātana ||
english: He who is undecaying, heavenly, whose foes are yet unborn — the self-powerful one approaches the wondrous Indra. Press the Soma, cook the food for him who is borne by prayer — set the much-praised one further forward.

sanskrit: ā yaḥ somena jaṭharam apipratāmanadat maghavā madhvo andhasaḥ | yad īm mṛgāya hantave mahāvadhaḥ sahasrabhṛṣṭim uśanā vadham yamat ||
english: He who has filled his belly with Soma — the bountiful one rejoiced at the sweet draught; when Uśanā aimed the great thousand-pointed weapon for him to slay the beast.

sanskrit: yo asmai ghraṁsa uta vā ya ūdhani somaṁ sunoti bhavati dyumām̐ ahaḥ | apāpa śakras tatanuṣṭim ūhati tanūśubhram maghavā yaḥ kavāsakhaḥ ||
english: He who presses Soma for him at the sun's heat or at the udder's fullness — that day becomes glorious. The blameless Śakra carries away his offspring-line; the bountiful one adorns his body who is the friend of the wise.

sanskrit: yasyāvadhīt pitaraṁ yasya mātaraṁ yasya śakro bhrātaraṁ nāta īṣate | vetīd v asya prayatā yataṁkaro na kilbiṣād īṣate vasva ākaraḥ ||
english: Whose father Śakra has slain, whose mother, whose brother — he does not care; he who prepares and exerts himself knows that source of wealth; the treasure-mine does not flee from impurity.

sanskrit: na pañcabhir daśabhir vaṣṭy ārabhaṁ nāsunvatā sacate puṣyatā cana | jināti ved amuya hanti vā dhunir ā devayum bhajati gomati vraje ||
english: He does not seek a hold with five or ten; he does not stay with him who neither presses Soma nor prospers. The restless one knows and conquers or slays; he allots to the god-seeking one a share in the cow-stall.

sanskrit: vitvakṣaṇaḥ samṛtau cakramāsajo 'sunvato viṣuṇaḥ sunvato vṛdhaḥ | indro viśvasya damitā vibhīṣaṇo yathāvaśaṁ nayati dāsam āryaḥ ||
english: He is the piercing one who has walked the battlefield as the unsent avenger — ruinous to the non-presser, increaser of the presser; Indra the subduer of all, the terrible, the noble one, leads the Dāsa according to his will.

sanskrit: sam īm paṇer ajati bhojanam muṣe vi dāśuṣe bhajati sūnaraṁ vasu | durge ca na dhriyate viśva ā puru jano yo asya taviṣīm acukrudhat ||
english: He drives together the Paṇi's food for the thief's benefit; he distributes the good wealth to the pious worshipper. In no stronghold anywhere can the people who have provoked his power be held fast.

sanskrit: saṁ yaj janau sudhanau viśvaśardhasāv aved indro maghavā goṣu śubhriṣu | yujaṁ hy anyam akṛta pravepa ny ud īṁ gavyaṁ sṛjate satvabhir dhoniḥ ||
english: When Indra the bountiful recognised the two who were well-armed, of all-conquering hosts, among the gleaming cows — he made one a yoke-fellow, set the other trembling, and the raging one unleashes the cattle-wealth with his warriors.

sanskrit: sahasrasām āgniveśiṁ gṛṇīṣe śatrim agna upamāṁ ketum aryaḥ ||
english: I praise the Āgniveśa who wins thousands, a hundred-fold, O Agni — the supreme banner, the noble hero.

sanskrit: yas te sādhiṣṭho 'vasa indra kratuṣ ṭam ā bhara | asmabhyaṁ carṣaṇīsahaṁ sasniṁ vājeṣu duṣṭaram ||
english: O Indra, bring that best plan of yours for our protection — that which conquers all peoples, that prize-winner hard to overcome in the contests.

sanskrit: yad indra te catastro yac chūra santi tisraḥ | yad vā pañca kṣitīnām avas tat su na ā bhara ||
english: Whether you have four, O Indra — or three, O hero — or five kinds of aid for the peoples, O Śūra — bring all that well to us.

sanskrit: ā te 'vo vareṇyaṁ vṛṣantamasya hūmahe | vṛṣajūtir hi jajñiṣa ābhūbhir indra turvaṇiḥ ||
english: We invoke your desirable, most bull-like aid; for you were born with the speed of a bull, O Indra the swift-striker, with overpowering forces.

sanskrit: vṛṣā hy asi rādhase jajñiṣe vṛṣṇi te śavaḥ | svakṣatraṁ te dhṛṣan manaḥ satrāham indra pauṁsyam ||
english: For you are a bull born for the giving of gifts; bull-like is your strength; your own rulership, your bold mind, O Indra, and your manhood that conquers all at once.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tam indra martyam amitrayantam adrivaḥ | sarvarathā śatakrato ni yāhi śavasas pate ||
english: O Indra, O stone-armed one, with your entire chariot force, O lord of a hundred powers, lord of might — tread down that mortal who acts as our enemy.

sanskrit: tvām id vṛtrahantama janāso vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | ugraṁ pūrvīṣu pūrvyaṁ havante vājasātaye ||
english: You alone, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, O foremost of old — the peoples who have strewn the sacred grass call upon you, the fierce, for the winning of prizes.

sanskrit: asmākam indra duṣṭaram puroyāvānam ājiṣu | sayāvānaṁ dhane-dhane vājayantam avā ratham ||
english: O Indra, favour our chariot that is hard to overcome, that goes in front in the races, that goes alongside in prize after prize, eager for booty.

sanskrit: asmākam indrehi no ratham avā puraṁdhyā | vayaṁ śaviṣṭha vāryaṁ divi śravo dadhīmahi divi stomam manāmahe ||
english: O Indra, come, protect our chariot with fullness of understanding; O mightiest, we would establish desirable fame in heaven; we would set our hymn of praise in heaven.

sanskrit: sa ā gamad indro yo vasūnāṁ ciketa dātuṁ dāmano rayīṇām | dhanvacaro na vaṁsagas tṛṣāṇaś cakamānaḥ pibatu dugdham aṁśum ||
english: May Indra come — he who takes notice of treasures, of giving riches from the giver's store; like a desert-wanderer or a reed-stalker thirsting and longing — let him drink the milked Soma-stalk.

sanskrit: ā te hanū harivaḥ śūra śipre ruhat somo na parvatasya pṛṣṭhe | anu tvā rājann arvato na hinvan gīrbhir madema puruhūta viśve ||
english: May Soma mount your two jaws, O hero of tawny horses, O Indra of beautiful lips, as on the back of a mountain; O king, urging you on like horses with our songs, may we all rejoice, O much-invoked.

sanskrit: cakraṁ na vṛttam puruhūta vepate mano bhiyā me amatir id adrivaḥ | rathād adhi tvā jaritā sadāvṛdha kuvin nu stoṣan maghavan purūvasuḥ ||
english: Like a turning wheel, O much-invoked, it trembles; my mind, my lack of wisdom quakes with fear, O stone-armed one. He who always grows stronger, the singer from his chariot — will he not praise you, O bountiful Purūvasu?

sanskrit: eṣa grāveva jaritā ta indreYarti vācam bṛhad āśuṣāṇaḥ | pra savyena maghavan yaṁsi rāyaḥ pra dakṣiṇid dha harivo mā vi venaḥ ||
english: This singer, O Indra, raises his voice like a pressing-stone, eagerly desiring the great reward. With your left hand, O bountiful one, push wealth forward; with your right — do not stray away, O lord of tawny horses.

sanskrit: vṛṣā tvā vṛṣaṇaṁ vardhatu dyaur vṛṣā vṛṣabhyāṁ vahase haribhyām | sa no vṛṣā vṛṣarathaḥ suśipra vṛṣakrato vṛṣā vajrin bhare dhāḥ ||
english: May the bull-heaven increase you the bull; the bull conveys you with the two bull-like tawny horses. So place us, O bull of beautiful lips, of bull-resolve, the bull, the thunderer, in the battle.

sanskrit: yo rohitau vājinau vājinīvān tribhiḥ śataiḥ sacamānāv adiṣṭa | yūne sam asmai kṣitayo namantāṁ śrutarathāya maruto duvoyā ||
english: He who ordained the two prize-winning red steeds to be accompanied by three hundreds — may the peoples bow to this young one of the renowned chariot; may the Maruts render service to him.

sanskrit: sam bhānunā yatate sūryasyājuhvāno ghṛtapṛṣṭhaḥ svañcāḥ ||
english: He who has a ghee-sprinkled back, well-formed, striving together with the lustre of the sun, pouring oblations — for him the undimmed Dawns have shone out, who says 'let us press Soma for Indra'.

sanskrit: samiḍḍhāgnir vanavat stīrṇabarhir yuktagrāvā sutasomo jarāte | grāvāṇo yasyeṣiraṁ vadanty ayad adhvaryur haviṣāva sindhu ||
english: Agni kindled, the sacred grass spread, the pressing-stones yoked, the Soma pressed — these are praised by the one whose pressing-stones speak vigorously; the adhvaryu has come with the oblation toward the river.

sanskrit: vadhūr iyam patim icchanty eti yā īṁ vahāte mahiṣīm iṣirām | āsya śravasyād ratha ā ca ghoṣāt purū sahasrā pari vartayāte ||
english: This bride goes seeking her husband, she who carries the vigorous great queen-cow; from his fame and from the sound of his chariot many thousands circle around.

sanskrit: na sa rājā vyathate yasmin indras tīvraṁ somam pibati gosakyāyam ||
english: That king does not waver in whose company Indra drinks the strong Soma together with the cows; he drives with warriors, smites Vṛtra, dwells among peoples, the fortunate one, fostering his name.

sanskrit: puṣyāt kṣeme abhi yoge bhavaty ubhe vṛtau saṁyatī saṁ jayāti | priyaḥ sūrye priyo agnā bhavati ya indrāya sutasomo dadāśat ||
english: He prospers in rest and in action; both enclosing seasons joining, he wins together. He becomes dear to the sun, dear to Agni — he who has presented pressed Soma to Indra.

sanskrit: uroṣ ṭa indra rādhaso vibhvī rātiḥ śatakrato | adhā no viśvacarṣaṇe dyumnā sukṣatra maṁhaya ||
english: O Indra, your giving from your ample bounty is all-pervading, O lord of a hundred powers; therefore, O all-people-beholding one, bestow splendours on us, O lord of good dominion.

sanskrit: yad īm indra śravāyyam iṣaṁ śaviṣṭha dadhiṣe | paprathe dīrghaśruttamaṁ hiraṇyavarṇa duṣṭaram ||
english: When you bestow, O mightiest Indra, the food worthy of renown — O one of golden colour, you spread it far, most renowned, hard to overcome.

sanskrit: śuṣmāso ye te adrivo mehanā ketasāpaḥ | ubhā devāv abhiṣṭaye divaś ca gmaś ca rājathaḥ ||
english: Your mighty surges, O stone-armed Indra, are like great floods with wise intention; O two gods, you rule both heaven and earth for the support of your worshippers.

sanskrit: uto no asya kasya cid dakṣasya tava vṛtrahan | asmabhyaṁ nṛmṇam ā bharāsmabhyaṁ nṛmaṇasyase ||
english: And from whatever power of yours, O slayer of Vṛtra — bring us manly force; you favour us with manly favour.

sanskrit: nū ta ābhir abhiṣṭibhis tava śarmaṁ chatakrato | indra syāma sugopāḥ śūra syāma sugopāḥ ||
english: Now with these your aids, O lord of a hundred powers, may we be in your shelter; O Indra, may we have good protection; O hero, may we have good protection.

sanskrit: yad indra citra mehanāsti tvādātam adrivaḥ | rādhas tan no vidadvasa ubhayāhasty ā bhara ||
english: O Indra, O wonderful Indra of mighty floods, whatever gift is yours — O stone-armed one, knowing it, bring that bounty to us with both hands, O lord of wealth.

sanskrit: yan manyase vareṇyam indra dyukṣaṁ tad ā bhara | vidyāma tasya te vayam akūpārasya dāvane ||
english: Whatever you think desirable, O Indra, the heavenly — bring that hither. May we know the giving of you, the boundless one.

sanskrit: yat te ditsu praradhyam mano asti śrutaṁ bṛhat | tena dṛḻhā cid adriva ā vājaṁ darṣi sātaye ||
english: Whatever mind is yours, inclined to give, heard of far and wide — with that, O stone-armed one, burst open even the firm strongholds for the winning of the prize.

sanskrit: maṁhiṣṭhaṁ vo maghonāṁ rājānaṁ carṣaṇīnām | indram upa praśastaye pūrvībhir jujuṣe giraḥ ||
english: For your praise we approach Indra the most munificent of the bountiful, the king of all peoples — he who has rejoiced in many hymns since ancient times.

sanskrit: asmā it kāvyaṁ vaca uktham indrāya śaṁsyam | tasmā u brahmavāhase giro vardhanty atra Yo giraḥ śumbhanty atrayaḥ ||
english: To him is directed the wise word, the utterance, the hymn recited for Indra; for him who bears the prayer, the Atris magnify their songs; the Atris adorn their songs.

sanskrit: ā yāhy adribhiḥ sutaṁ somaṁ somapate piba | vṛṣann indra vṛṣabhir vṛtrahantama ||
english: Come with the pressing-stones to the pressed Soma; drink, O lord of Soma; O bull Indra, with the bulls — O greatest slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: vṛṣā grāvā vṛṣā mado vṛṣā somo ayaṁ sutaḥ | vṛṣann indra vṛṣabhir vṛtrahantama ||
english: The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull; this pressed Soma is a bull — O bull Indra, with the bulls, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: vṛṣā tvā vṛṣaṇam huve vajriñ citrābhir ūtibhiḥ | vṛṣann indra vṛṣabhir vṛtrahantama ||
english: As a bull I invoke you the bull, O Indra the thunderer, with wonderful aids — O bull Indra, with the bulls, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: ṛjīṣī vajrī vṛṣabhas turāṣāṭ śuṣmī rājā vṛtrahā somapāvā | yuktvā haribhyām upa yāsad arvāṅ mādhyaṁdine savane matsad indraḥ ||
english: He who possesses the Ṛjīṣa, the thunderer, the bull, the overwhelmer of foes, the powerful, the king, the Vṛtra-slayer, the Soma-drinker — having yoked the two tawny horses let Indra come hither and rejoice at the midday pressing.

sanskrit: yat tvā sūrya svarbhānus tamasāvidhyad āsuraḥ | akṣetravid yathā mugdho bhuvanāny adīdhayuḥ ||
english: When Svarbhānu the Asura pierced you, O Sūrya, with darkness — like one foolish and ignorant of the region — the worlds were bewildered.

sanskrit: svarbhānor adha yad indra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan | gūḷhaṁ sūryaṁ tamasāpavratena turīyeṇa brahmaṇāvinad atriḥ ||
english: When, O Indra, Svarbhānu's deceits — operating from below the sky — struck Sūrya down, Atri by his fourth prayer found the sun hidden by enveloping darkness.

sanskrit: mā mām imaṁ tava santam atra irasyā drugdho bhiyasā ni gārīt | tvam mitro asi satyarādhās tau me hāvatam varuṇaś ca rājā ||
english: Let not the deceitful malicious one swallow me here in fear — me who am yours. You are Mitra of true bounty; both Mitra and king Varuṇa shall come to my aid.

sanskrit: grāvṇo brahmā yuyujānaḥ sapayan kīriṇā devān namasopośikṣan | atriḥ sūryasya divi cakṣur ādhāt svarbhānor apa māyā aghukṣat ||
english: The priest straining at the pressing-stones, honouring the gods with song and supplication — Atri placed the eye of the sun back in heaven and wiped away the deceits of Svarbhānu.

sanskrit: yaṁ vai sūryaṁ svarbhānus tamasāvidhyad āsuraḥ | atrayas tam anv avindan na hy anye aśaknuvan ||
english: The sun that Svarbhānu the Asura pierced with darkness — the Atris found him; for no others could do it.

sanskrit: ko nu vām mitrāvaruṇāv ṛtāyan divo vā mahaḥ pārthivasya vā de | ṛtasya vā sadasi trāsīthāṁ no yajñāyate vā paśuṣo na vājān ||
english: Who now, O Mitra and Varuṇa, following truth — from great heaven or from earth — would protect us at the seat of truth, or bring prizes like cattle to the sacrificer?

sanskrit: te no mitro varuṇo aryamāyur indra ṛbhukṣā maruto juṣanta | namobhir vā ye dadhate suvṛktiṁ stomaṁ rudrāya mīḻhuṣe sajoṣāḥ ||
english: May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra the strong, the Maruts favour us — those who with obeisances or with fair hymns together uphold the praise-song to the bountiful Rudra with one accord.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ yeṣṭhāśvinā huvadhyai vātasya patman rathyasya puṣṭau | uta vā divo asurasya manma prāndhāṁsīva yajyave bharadhvam ||
english: O Aśvins, I would invoke you both to come hither — on the path of the wind, in the welfare of the chariot. Or bear toward the worshipper the thought of the mighty lord of heaven, as one would bring food to the blind.

sanskrit: pra sakṣaṇo divyaḥ kaṇvahotā trito divaḥ sajoṣā vāto agniḥ | pūṣā bhagaḥ prabhṛthe viśvabhojā ājiṁ na jagmur āśvaśvatamāḥ ||
english: The divine Kaṇva-Hotr who follows on without pause, Trita of the sky in accord, Vāyu, Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the all-nourishing one at the offering-time — they have come to the race like the swiftest of horses.

sanskrit: pra vo rayiṁ yuktāśvam bharadhvaṁ rāya eṣe 'vase dadhīta dhīḥ | suśeva evair auśijasya hotā ye va evā marutas turāṇām ||
english: Bring forward for yourselves the wealth with harnessed horses; let thought be placed in the seeking of wealth for protection. The Hotr of the son of Uśij — with the aids that are truly gracious — these Maruts are the speedy ones.

sanskrit: pra vo vāyuṁ rathayujaṁ kṛṇudhvam pra devaṁ vipram panitāram arkaiḥ | iṣudhyava ṛtasāpaḥ puraṁdhīr vasvīr no atra patnīr ā dhiye dhuḥ ||
english: Make Vāyu come forward, the chariot-yoker; make the divine, inspired one worthy of praise come forward with hymns. May those who strive like arrows, who obtain the truth, the enriching, the understanding patrons — may the good ladies place themselves in thought for us here.

sanskrit: upa va eṣe vandyebhiḥ śūṣaiḥ pra yahvī divaś citayadbhir arkaiḥ | uṣāsānaktā viduṣīva viśvam ā hā vahato martyāya yajñam ||
english: In her approach to you with praisable vigours, in the great Heaven's illumining with hymns — Dawn-and-Night, as if knowing all, carry the sacrifice here to the mortal.

sanskrit: abhi vo arce poṣyāvato nṝn vāstoṣ patiṁ tvaṣṭāraṁ rarāṇaḥ | dhanyā sajoṣā dhiṣaṇā namobhir vanapatīm̐r oṣadhī rāya eṣe ||
english: I sing for you prosperous, wealth-giving men — for the Lord of the Dwelling and for Tvaṣṭṛ who gives freely; may the bountiful Dhiṣaṇā, in harmony, with obeisances — may forest trees and herbs seek wealth.

sanskrit: tuje nas tane parvatāḥ santu svaitavo ye vasavo na vīrāḥ | panita āptyo yajataḥ sadā no vardhān naḥ śaṁsaṁ naryo abhiṣṭau ||
english: For our offspring and lineage may the mountains be ours — those white-gleaming Vasava-like heroes; worthy of praise, the Āptya, the reverend one, ever among us — may he, the manly, increase our fame in our conquest.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇo astoṣi bhūmyasya garbhaṁ trito napātam apāṁ suvṛkti | gṛṇīte agnir etarī na śūṣair śociṣkeśo ni riṇāti vanā ||
english: I have praised the embryo of the bull-like earth; Trita, the child of the waters, with fair hymns. Agni raises his voice with vigours like a racer; he of the fiery hair shatters the forests.

sanskrit: kathā mahe rudriyāya bravāma kad rāye cikituṣe bhagāya | āpa oṣadhīr uta no 'vantu dyaur vanā girayo vṛkṣakeśāḥ ||
english: How shall we speak to the great Rudriya? How to Bhaga who has discernment about wealth? May the waters, the plants, and heaven protect us — forests and mountains whose hair is trees.

sanskrit: śṛṇotu na ūrjām patir giraḥ sa nabhas tarīyām̐ iṣiraḥ parijmā | śṛṇvanty āpaḥ puro na śubhrāḥ pari srucoho babṛhāṇasyādreḥ ||
english: May the lord of nourishments hear our songs; may the energetic, all-surrounding one cross the cloud. The bright waters like forts listen; they flow around the ladle of the pressing mountain.

sanskrit: vidā cin nu mahānto ye va evā bravāma dasmā vāryaṁ dadhānāḥ | vayaś ca na subhva ā ava yanti kṣubhā martam anuyataṁ vadhasnaiḥ ||
english: Let the great ones truly know — those to whom we speak thus, who hold the desirable; even beautiful birds come down toward us, and they shake the mortal who goes along with their striking weapons.

sanskrit: ā daivyāni pārthivāni janmāpaś cācchā sumakhāya vocam | vardhatāṁ dyāvo giraś candrāgrā udā vardhantām abhiṣātā arṇāḥ ||
english: I have spoken toward the divine and earthly births, toward the waters for the sake of the gracious one. May the heavens and the bright-crested hymns increase; may the conquering floods rise up.

sanskrit: pade-pade me jarimā ni dhāyi varūtrī vā śakrā yā pāyubhiś ca | siṣaktu mātā mahī rasā naḥ smat sūribhir ṛjuhasta ṛjuvaniḥ ||
english: At every step my old age has been placed; but the powerful sheltering one with her guards is there. May the great mother Earth, the rich in sap, remain with us — the straight-handed, straight-bountiful one, among the wise patrons.

sanskrit: kathā dāśema namasā sudānūn evayā maruto achoktau praśravaso maruto achoktau | mā no 'hir budhnyo riṣe dhād asmākam bhūd upamātivaniḥ ||
english: How shall we worship with obeisances the generous Maruts of good hearing — the Maruts of good hearing whose call speeds forward? May the serpent Ahi Budhnya not put us to harm; may he be the highest increaser for us.

sanskrit: iti cin nu prajāyai paśumatyai devāso vanate martyo va ā devāso vanate martyo vaḥ | atrā śivāṁ tanvo dhāsim asyā jarāṁ cin me nirṛtir jagrasīta ||
english: Thus indeed a mortal wins from you gods, O gods, for his offspring rich in cattle — the mortal wins from you, O gods. May he establish the auspicious body-share here; even my old age let Nirṛti devour.

sanskrit: tāṁ vo devāḥ sumatiṁ ūrjayantīm iṣam aśyāma vasavaḥ śasā goḥ | sā naḥ sudānur mṛḻayantī devī prati dravantī suvitāya gamyāḥ ||
english: That favour of yours, O gods, that strengthening refreshment — may we Vasus attain it through the recitation of the cow. May that divine generous goddess, bestowing grace, come running toward us for our good fortune.

sanskrit: abhi na iḷā yūthasya mātā sman nadībhir urvaśī vā gṛṇātu | urvaśī vā bṛhaddivā gṛṇānābhyūrṇvānā prabhṛthasyāyoḥ ||
english: May Iḷā, the mother of the herd, praise us here together with the rivers; or may Urvaśī praise us; or Bṛhaddivā-Urvaśī, praising and spreading forth for the longevity of the offering.

sanskrit: siṣaktu na ūrjavyasya puṣṭeḥ ||
english: May she remain with us for the nourishment of the vigorous one.

sanskrit: pra śaṁtamā varuṇaṁ dīdhitī gīr mitram bhagam aditiṁ nūnam aśyāḥ | pṛṣadyoniḥ pañcahotā śṛṇotv atūrtapanthā asuro mayobhuḥ ||
english: May my most pleasant thought and song now reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Bhaga, and Aditi. May the five-Hotr of the dappled source, the unimpeded path-maker, the mighty Asura, the source of bliss, hear.

sanskrit: prati me stomam aditir jagṛbhyāt sūnuṁ na mātā hṛdyaṁ suśevam | brahma priyaṁ devahitaṁ yad asty aham mitre varuṇe yan mayobhu ||
english: May Aditi receive my praise-song as a mother receives her dear, gracious son. The prayer that is dear, established by the gods, that which is a source of bliss — may I place it in Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: ud īraya kavitamaṁ kavīnām unattai nam abhi madhvā ghṛtena | sa no vasūni prayatā hitāni candrāṇi devaḥ savitā suvāti ||
english: Raise up the most wise among the wise; anoint him with honey and with ghee. May the divine Savitṛ set flowing for us abundant wealth, granted and established, and lovely things.

sanskrit: sam indra ṇo manasā neṣi gobhiḥ saṁ sūribhir haravaḥ saṁ svasti | sam brahmaṇā devahitaṁ yad asti saṁ devānāṁ sumatyā yajñiyānām ||
english: O Indra, guide us together with mind and with cows, with patrons, with welfare; bring us together with the prayer that is established by the gods, with the favour of the gods worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: devo bhagaḥ savitā rāyo aṁśa indro vṛtrasya saṁjito dhanānām | ṛbhukṣā vāja uta vā puraṁdhir avantu no amṛtāsas turāsaḥ ||
english: Divine Bhaga, Savitṛ the sharer of wealth, Indra the conqueror of Vṛtra and of riches, Ṛbhukṣa and Vāja, and Puraṁdhi — may the immortal swift ones protect us.

sanskrit: marutvatoḥ apratītasya jiṣṇor ajūryataḥ pra bravāmā kṛtāni | na te pūrve maghavan nāparāso na vīryaṁ nūtanaḥ kaś canāpa ||
english: We proclaim the deeds of him with the Maruts, the unconquered victor, who ages not. Neither those who came before, O bountiful one, nor those who came after, nor yet any new one has equalled your heroic might.

sanskrit: upa stuhi prathamaṁ ratnadheyam bṛhaspatiṁ sanitāraṁ dhanānām | yaḥ śaṁsate stuvate śambhaviṣṭhaḥ purūvasur āgamaj johurvānam ||
english: Praise first the giver of jewels, Bṛhaspati, the winner of riches; he who is most beneficent to him who hymns and praises — the one rich in many goods shall come to him who calls.

sanskrit: tavotibhiḥ sacamānā ariṣṭā bṛhaspate maghavānaḥ suvīrāḥ | ye aśvadā uta vā santi godā ye vastradāḥ subhagās teṣu rāyaḥ ||
english: Protected by your aids, O Bṛhaspati, the bountiful ones go unharmed, the heroes; those who give horses, who give cows, who give garments — among those fortunate ones is wealth.

sanskrit: visarmāṇaṁ kṛṇuhi vittam eṣāṁ ye bhuñjate apṛṇanto na ukthaiḥ | apavratān prasave vāvṛdhānān brahmadviṣaḥ sūryād yāvayasva ||
english: Scatter the possessions of those who enjoy without giving, who make no offering with hymns. Drive away from the sun those who transgress the law, who are waxing in arrogance, who hate the sacred word.

sanskrit: ya ohate rakṣaso devavītāv acakrebhis tam maruto ni yāta | yo vaḥ śamīṁ śaśamānasya nindāt tuccyān kāmān karate siṣvidānaḥ ||
english: Him who opposes at the gods' feast with those who have no wheels — tread him down, O Maruts. He who would blame the laboured labour of one who has laboured for you — let that sweating one achieve only petty desires.

sanskrit: tam u ṣṭuhi yaḥ sviṣuḥ sudhanvā yo viśvasya kṣayati bheṣajasya | yakṣvā mahe saumanasāya rudraṁ namobhir devam asuraṁ duvasya ||
english: Praise him who has good arrows, a good bow, who rules over all medicines; worship Rudra with obeisances for great grace — honour the divine, the mighty Asura.

sanskrit: damūnaso apasat ye suhastā vṛṣṇaḥ patnīr nadyo vibhvataṣṭāḥ | sarasvatī bṛhaddivota rākā daśasyantīr varivasyantu śubhrāḥ ||
english: The household-dwelling, active ones of good hands — the wives of the bull, the rivers shaped by the Pervader — may Sarasvatī and Bṛhaddivā, and Rākā, the bright ones, show favour and do their service.

sanskrit: pra sū mahe suśaraṇāya medhāṁ giram bhare navyasīṁ jāyamānām | ya āhanā duhitur vakṣaṇāsu rūpā mināno akṛṇod idaṁ naḥ ||
english: I now bring wisdom, a newly born song, to the great well-sheltered one. He who, striking the daughter's flanks with his arms, marring her forms, fashioned this for us.

sanskrit: pra suṣṭutiḥ stanayantaṁ ruvantam iḷas patim jaritar nūnam aśyāḥ | yo abdimām̐ udanimām̐ iyarti pra vidyutā rodasī ukṣamāṇaḥ ||
english: O singer, may your perfect praise now reach the Lord of Iḷā who thunders and roars — he who drives forth the cloud-full, water-full one, and rains upon the two worlds with lightning.

sanskrit: eṣa stomo mārutaṁ śardho acchā rudrasya sūnūm̐r yuvayanūm̐r ud aśyāḥ | kāmo rāye havate mā svasy upa stuhi pṛṣadaśvām̐ ayāsaḥ ||
english: May this hymn of praise now reach the Marutic troop, the sons of Rudra, the youthful; desire calls me for wealth and welfare — praise without wearying the Maruts of dappled horses.

sanskrit: praiṣa stomaḥ pṛthivīm antariṣaṁ vanapatīm̐r oṣadhī rāye aśyāḥ | devo-devaḥ suhavo bhūtu mahyam mā no mātā pṛthivī durmatadhāt ||
english: May this hymn of praise reach earth and atmosphere and the forest trees and the plants for wealth. May each and every god be easy to invoke for me; may mother Earth not put us in an evil mind.

sanskrit: urau devā anibādhe syāma ||
english: May we be in a wide, unobstructed space, O gods.

sanskrit: sam aśvinor avasā nūtanena mayobhuvā supraṇītī gamema | ā no rayiṁ vahatam ota vīrān ā viśvāny amṛtā saubhagāni ||
english: With the new aid of the Aśvins, the blissful, the well-guiding, may we meet together; bring us wealth and heroes; bring us, O immortals, all good fortunes.

sanskrit: ā dhenavah payasā tūrṇyarthā amardhantīr upa no yantu madhvā | maho rāye bṛhatīḥ sapta vipro mayobhuvo jaritā johovīti ||
english: May the milk-cows come swiftly to us, overflowing with milk, undiminishing, with sweetness; the inspired singer calls upon the seven great sources of bliss for great wealth.

sanskrit: ā suṣṭutī namasā vartayadhyai dyāvā vājāya pṛthivī amṛdhre | pitā mātā madhuvacāḥ suhastā bhare-bhare no yaśasāv aviṣṭām ||
english: To turn the perfect praise with obeisances — may undiminishing Heaven and Earth come to our prize-contest; the father and mother of honeyed speech, of good hands — may the two glorious ones protect us in every contest.

sanskrit: adhvaryavaś cakṛvāṁso madhūni pra vāyave bharata cāru śukram | hoteva naḥ prathamaḥ pāhy asya deva madhvo rarimā te madāya ||
english: O adhvaryus who have prepared the sweet things, bring the lovely bright one to Vāyu; protect us first as does a Hotr; O god, we have poured sweet drink for your exhilaration.

sanskrit: daśa kṣipo yuñjate bāhū adrim somasya yā śamitārā suhastā | madhvo rasaṁ sugabhastir giriṣṭhāṁ caniścadad duduhe śukram aṁśuḥ ||
english: Ten pressing-fingers yoke the arms to the stone — those two skilled dressers of the Soma. The stalk standing on the mountain, the well-armed one, has milked forth the bright sweet essence, drop by drop.

sanskrit: asāvi te jujuṣāṇāya soma kratve dakṣāya bṛhate madāya | harī rathe sudhurā yoge arvāg indra priyā kṛṇuhi hūyamānaḥ ||
english: The Soma has been pressed for you who are pleased by it, for wisdom, for great discernment, for exhilaration; the two well-yoked tawny horses in your chariot — make them come hither, O Indra, when called.

sanskrit: ā no mahīm aramatim sajoṣā gnāṁ devīṁ namasā rātahavyām | madhor madāya bṛhatīm ṛtajñām āgne vaha pathibhir devayānaiḥ ||
english: Bring hither to us great Aramatī in harmony, the divine lady who accepts oblations with obeisances; for the exhilaration of the sweet, the great one who knows the truth — bring her, O Agni, on the god-going paths.

sanskrit: añjanti yam prathayanto na viprā vapāvantaṁ nāgninā tapantaḥ | pitur na putra upasi preṣṭha ā gharmo agniṁ ṛtayann asādi ||
english: Him whom the inspired ones anoint, spreading him out as it were, the one with the fatty omentum, not burning with fire — like a dear son in his father's presence, Gharma has been established, ordering Agni with truth.

sanskrit: acchā mahī bṛhatī śaṁtamā gīr dūto na gantv aśvinā huvadhyai | mayobhuvā sarathā yātam arvāg gantam nidhiṁ dhuram āṇir na nābhim ||
english: May the great, ample, most gracious song go like a messenger to summon the Aśvins hither; come on the same chariot, you sources of bliss; come to the treasure and the draught-bar like a pin to the nave.

sanskrit: pra tavyaso namauktiṁ turasyāham pūṣṇa uta vā yora adikṣi | yā rādhasā coditārā matīnāṁ yā vājasya draviṇodā uta tman ||
english: I have looked toward the praise-offering of the mighty, the swift Pūṣan and of Vāyu — who are the impellers of thoughts with bounty, who of themselves are the givers of wealth of the prize.

sanskrit: ā nāmabhir maruto vakṣi viśvān ā rūpebhir jātavedo huvānaḥ | yajñaṁ giro jaritoḥ suṣṭutiṁ ca viśve ganta maruto viśva ūtī ||
english: With the names of all the Maruts bring them hither, with their forms, O Jātavedas, invoking them; may the Maruts come to the sacrifice and the songs and perfect praise of the singer — all with all aids.

sanskrit: ā no divo bṛhataḥ parvataad ā sarasvatī yajatā gantu yajñam | havaṁ devī jujuṣāṇā ghṛtācī śagmāṁ no vācam uśatī śṛṇotu ||
english: From the great heaven, from the mountain, may the holy Sarasvatī come to our sacrifice; may the divine, ghee-bright one who finds pleasure in our invocation, in her longing, hear our auspicious speech.

sanskrit: ā vedhAsam nīlapṛṣṭham bṛhantam bṛhaspatiṁ sadane sādayadhvam | sādadyoniṁ dama ā dīdivāṁsaṁ hiraṇyavarṇam aruṣaṁ sapema ||
english: Seat great Bṛhaspati, the ordainer, the blue-backed, the ample, in the seat; may we approach him who sits established in his home, who blazes in the house, golden-coloured and ruddy.

sanskrit: ā dharṇasir bṛhaddivo rarāṇo viśvebhir gantv omabhir huvānaḥ | gnā vasāna oṣadhīr amṛdhras tridhātuśṛṅgo vṛṣabho vayodhāḥ ||
english: May Dharṇasi the great-heavenly one, ever generous, come with all his aids, being invoked; wearing the divine ladies and the plants undiminishing — the triple-natured-horned bull, the sustainer of life.

sanskrit: mātuṣ pade parame śukra āyor vipanyavo rāspirāso agman | suśevyaṁ namasā rātahavyāḥ śiśum mṛjanty āyavo na vāse ||
english: At the highest station of the mother, the bright one, the Āyus, the eloquent singers with glad voices have come; those who accept oblations with obeisances for gracious shelter — the Āyus cleanse the child as if in a garment.

sanskrit: bṛhad vayo bṛhate tubhyam agne dhiyājuro mithunāsaḥ sacanta | devo-devaḥ suhavo bhūtu mahyam mā no mātā pṛthivī durmatadhāt ||
english: O Agni, great nourishment — may the pairs who are not wearied by thought stay together with you the great; may each and every god be easy to invoke for me; may mother Earth not put us in an evil mind.

sanskrit: urau devā anibādhe syāma ||
english: May we be in a wide, unobstructed space, O gods.

sanskrit: sam aśvinor avasā nūtanena mayobhuvā supraṇītī gamema | ā no rayiṁ vahatam ota vīrān ā viśvāny amṛtā saubhagāni ||
english: With the new aid of the Aśvins, the blissful, the well-guiding, may we meet together; bring us wealth and heroes; bring us, O immortals, all good fortunes.

sanskrit: tam pratnathā pūrvathā viśvathemathā jyeṣṭhatātim barhiṣadaṁ svārvidam | pratīcīnaṁ vṛjanaṁ dohase girāśuṁ jayantam anu yāsu vardhase ||
english: Him of ancient fashion, of primeval fashion, of universal fashion — him the eldest who sits on the sacred grass, who finds the light — the swift victor of the turned community, whom you magnify with your song for milking.

sanskrit: śriye sudṛśīr upārasya yāḥ svar virocamānaḥ kakubhām acodate | sugopā asi na dabhāya sukrato paro māyābhir ṛta āsa nāma te ||
english: For beauty those well-visible ones of the high — shining with heavenly light he impels the quarters. You are a good shepherd; you are not to be deceived, O of good resolve; by your arts you have been called by the name of truth.

sanskrit: atyaṁ haviḥ sacate sac ca dhātu cāriṣṭagātuḥ sa hotā sahobhariḥ | prasarsrāṇo anu barhir vṛṣā śiśur madhye yuvājaro visruhā hitaḥ ||
english: The oblation follows the steed and nourishment follows; he of unimpeded course, the Hotr who bears might — the bull-calf gliding along the sacred grass, young in the middle, ageless, placed amid the outstretched ones.

sanskrit: pra va ete suyujo yāmann iṣṭaye nīcīr amuṣmai yamya ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | suyantuibhiḥ sarvaśāsair abhīśubhiḥ krivir nāmāni pravaṇe muṣāyati ||
english: These well-yoked ones advance toward this worship on their course, the downward-inclined ones, to be guided, who increase the truth; with good drivers, with all-directing reins, Krivi steals the names on the downward slope.

sanskrit: saṁjarbhurāṇas tarubhiḥ sutegṛbhaṁ vayākinaṁ cittagarbhāsu susvaruḥ ||
english: Resounding together with the young ones, grasping the pressed drink, the winged one who has thought within beautiful-sounding women — he sounds well.

sanskrit: yādṛg eva dadṛśe tādṛg ucyate saṁ chāyayā dadhire sidhrayāpsv ā | mahīm asmabhyam uruṣām uru jrayo bṛhat suvīram anapacyutaṁ sahaḥ ||
english: As he was seen, so he is described; they placed him together with his shadow, with the sycamore, in the waters. Great, far-reaching, of wide expanse, great, truly heroic, unimpaired strength for us.

sanskrit: vety agrur janivān vā ati spṛdhaḥ samaryatā manasā sūryaḥ kaviḥ | ghraṁsaṁ rakṣantam pari viśvato gayam asmākaṁ śarma vanavat svāvasuḥ ||
english: The early-rising one, born of woman or overcoming rivals, the sun, the sage, with rival-conquering mind — may our well-self-rich one win shelter for us all around, guarding the glowing heat and home.

sanskrit: jyāyāṁsam asya yatunasya ketunā ṛṣisvaram carati yāsu nāma te | yādṛśmin dhāyi tam apasyayā vidad ya u svayaṁ vahate so araṁ karat ||
english: Greater than this Yatu by his banner — the seer's voice moves among those where your name is; what was placed therein — whoever finds that one through watchfulness — he who carries by himself will do what is fitting.

sanskrit: samudram āsām ava tasthe agrimā na riṣyati savanaṁ yasmin āyatā | atrā na hārdi kravaṇasya rejate yatrā matir vidyate pūtabandhanī ||
english: The foremost of these has taken its stand at the ocean; the pressing to which it has come is not harmed. There the heart of the raw-flesh eater does not tremble — where the thought is found with its pure bond.

sanskrit: sa hi kṣatrasya manasasya cittibhir evāvadasya yajatasya sadreḥ | avatsārasya spṛṇavāma raṇvabhiḥ śaviṣṭhaṁ vājaṁ viduṣā cid ardhyam ||
english: For by his understanding of sovereignty, of mind, of thought — the single-voiced, the reverend, the joint one — we win with joyful songs the great prize of Avatsāra, the mightiest, worthy of the wise man's share.

sanskrit: śyena āsām aditiḥ kakṣyo mado viśvavārasya yajatasya māyinaḥ | sam anyam-anyam arthayanti etave vidur viṣāṇam paripānam anti te ||
english: The eagle is Aditi among these — the intoxicating drink of the armpit, of the all-desirable, the reverend, the māyā-wielding one; they direct one another and the next to go forward; they know the horn, the all-protective — it is near them.

sanskrit: sadāpṛṇo yajato vi dviṣo vadhīd bāhuvṛktaḥ śrutavit taryo vaḥ sacā | ubhā sa varā praty eti bhāti ca yad īṁ gaṇam bhajate suprayāvabhiḥ ||
english: The ever-giving, the reverend, has slain the enemy; the arm-embraced, the knowledge-knowing one, swift among you together — he goes toward both the choices and shines; when he partakes of the troop with good impulsions.

sanskrit: sutaṁbharo yajamānasya satpatir viśvāsām ūdhaḥ sa dhiyām udañcanaḥ | bharad dhenū rasavac chiśriye payo 'nubruvāṇo adhy eti na svapan ||
english: The bearer of the pressed drink, the true lord of the sacrificer, the udder of all thoughts, the uplifter — carrying the milk-cows bringing rich, sweet milk — repeating and going forward, he does not sleep.

sanskrit: yo jāgāra tam ṛcaḥ kāmayante yo jāgāra tam u sāmāni yanti | yo jāgāra tam ayaṁ soma āha tavāham asmi sakhye nyokāḥ ||
english: He who keeps awake — the Ṛc verses desire him; he who keeps awake — the Sāman chants approach him; he who keeps awake — this Soma says to him: 'I am yours, dwelling in your friendship'.

sanskrit: agnir jāgāra tam ṛcaḥ kāmayante 'gnir jāgāra tam u sāmāni yanti | agnir jāgāra tam ayaṁ soma āha tavāham asmi sakhye nyokāḥ ||
english: Agni keeps awake — the Ṛc verses desire him; Agni keeps awake — the Sāman chants approach him; Agni keeps awake — this Soma says to him: 'I am yours, dwelling in your friendship'.
